_doc: The model taxonomy's vocabulary: each model has one category, its shelf, and any tags, terms grouped by facet. Every term carries its one-line meaning. Why it is semi-closed, and how a term is requested and added, is in models/TAXONOMY.md.

categories.ammunition: Cartridges, rounds, shells, spent cases and the boxes and cans made to hold them.
categories.arcana: Magical and occult objects: wands, rune tablets, charms, ritual gear.
categories.armour: Protective wear and shields: helmets, armoured vests, plate, powered armour.
categories.body-parts: Bodies and pieces of them that are not animated actors: the player's body parts, severed limbs, remains.
categories.clothing: Garments, headwear, footwear and gloves worn for cover, warmth or style rather than protection.
categories.containers: Things made to hold other things: cans, bottles, boxes, crates, bags, backpacks, fuel cans.
categories.creatures: Animated generated actors with a body and pose clips: creatures, the undead, the player.
categories.documents: Written and printed matter: notebooks, books, notes, letters, maps, signs to read.
categories.electrical: Powered devices and their components: radios, batteries, wire, fuses, appliances, gadgets.
categories.food: Food and drink, fresh or packaged, sealed, opened or emptied.
categories.furniture: Furnishings: seats, tables, beds, mattresses, shelves, cabinets, lockers.
categories.household: Domestic utensils and small household objects: kitchenware, cleaning gear, decor.
categories.keys: Keys, keycards and other tokens that open a lock or a door.
categories.lighting: Light sources and fire starters: torches, lamps, candles, flashlights, lighters, matches.
categories.machinery: Workshop and industrial machines and engines: compressors, presses, stationary saws, furnaces, generators.
categories.materials: Raw and crafting materials and loose hardware: planks, sticks, nails, tape, cord, wax, scrap, hinges.
categories.medical: Medicine and first aid: drugs, bandages, antiseptics, medical instruments.
categories.nature: Natural objects as found: rocks, plants, logs, shells, bones lying loose.
categories.recreation: Toys, games, sports gear and musical instruments.
categories.structures: Building elements and fixtures: walls, doors, windows, fences, barriers, signs on posts.
categories.tools: Hand and power tools carried to do work: hammers, saws, axes, pliers, jacks, repair kits.
categories.vehicle-parts: Parts and fittings of vehicles: shells, panels, doors, glass, wheels, axles, engines, seats, lamps.
categories.weapon-parts: Pieces of weapons and their accessories: magazines, receivers, barrels, stocks, sights, suppressors, slings, mounts.
categories.weapons: Whole weapons: firearms, melee weapons, explosives and traps.

fit.meaning: How a worn model is shaped: as worn on the shared player body rather than lying loose. A loose model has no fit.

terms.worn: Shaped to sit on the shared player body.
terms.over-jacket: Shaped to sit over a jacket on the shared player body, a second layer.

material.meaning: The one or two materials the model mostly reads as, not every material in it.

terms.fabric: Woven or knitted cloth, felt, rope and cord.
terms.metal: Any metal: steel, iron, bronze, copper, aluminium, gold.
terms.plant: Unworked plant matter: leaves, straw, bark, reed, fibre.

setting.meaning: The era or genre a model belongs to. Untagged reads as no particular setting.

terms.prehistoric: Stone-age making: knapped stone, digging sticks, lashed hafts.
terms.ancient: Classical and bronze-age antiquity: bronze arms, Greek and Roman gear.
terms.medieval: The middle ages and other pre-gunpowder feudal settings: plate, mail, kite shields.
terms.modern: The present day, from roughly the twentieth century: the everyday world.
terms.sci-fi: Future technology: powered armour, energy weapons, starship gear.
terms.fantasy: Magic and myth: wands, enchanted gear, wizard dress.

slot.meaning: Where on the body the model is worn; a worn set's pieces each name the part they cover.

terms.head: On the head: hats, helmets, hoods, circlets.
terms.face: Over the face or eyes: masks, goggles, visors.
terms.neck: Round the neck: scarves, collars, necklaces.
terms.torso: On the trunk: shirts, jackets, vests, body armour.
terms.arms: On the upper or lower arms: sleeves, bracers.
terms.waist: At the waist or hips: belts, waist packs.
terms.legs: On the hips and legs: trousers, leg guards.
terms.feet: On the feet: shoes, boots and their shafts.
terms.back: On the back or slung over a shoulder: backpacks, slings, quivers.

state.meaning: A condition a model shows that sets it apart from the plain, whole object.

terms.abandoned: Left to decay: weathered, rusted, flat tyres, broken glass.
terms.crashed: Damaged by a crash or collision but still whole: crumpled, jackknifed.
terms.wrecked: A total wreck, beyond repair: stripped, torn apart or burnt to the frame, not just damaged.
terms.broken: Broken or dead and no longer working.

vehicle-body.meaning: The body or airframe type of the vehicle a model is or belongs to.

terms.car: Cars: hatchbacks, saloons, estates, coupés, SUVs and 4x4s.
terms.truck: Lorries and trucks with a cab: box, flatbed, tipper, tanker, tractor units.
terms.trailer: Trailers and caravans, towed rather than driven.

vehicle-role.meaning: The service or work the vehicle a model is or belongs to is built for, whatever its body.

terms.emergency: Ambulance, fire, police and rescue service.
terms.farm: Farm work: tractors, harvesters, livestock trailers.
terms.construction: Construction and heavy plant: excavators, cranes, rollers, forklifts.

weapon.meaning: The weapon class a model is or serves, so a class finds its weapons, parts and ammunition together.

terms.energy: Weapons that fire energy or plasma rather than solid rounds.
terms.blade: Edged weapons that cut or stab: knives, swords, machetes.
terms.blunt: Weapons that strike: bats, clubs, maces, pipes.
terms.polearm: Weapons on a long shaft: spears, poles, halberds.
terms.trap: Traps set to catch or wound.
